# Skyro<>GrowthBook - Demo
Date: 2026-10-29 | Duration: 34.369998931884766m

## Summary
The discussion evaluated using one self-hosted, warehouse-native GrowthBook instance with regional separation through projects, roles, and environments. Business users need to create experiments, target audiences, define metrics, and review results independently, while the current regional use is mainly technical feature flagging. Experiments can link feature flags to control and treatment behavior, use user or account identifiers, apply targeting rules, and analyze conversion, lift, winning probability, and dimensions such as country or plan. Exposure events would flow through the existing analytics pipeline into the warehouse, where reusable SQL metrics could connect assignments with business outcomes. Saved groups support CSV or text-based user lists, but direct Snowflake retrieval remains unconfirmed. The team requires least-privilege access to selected tables and a security review. Dmitriy's team will prepare experiment and metric tables, configure an initial experiment, and request review. Jake offered enterprise access and implementation support, while Dmitriy will collect feedback and follow up.

## Keywords
Experimentation platform, Feature flags, Warehouse-native analytics, Multi-region access control, Experiment metrics, Snowflake data integration

# Skyro<>GrowthBook - POC Training
Date: 2026-11-10 | Duration: 50.130001068115234m

## Summary
The discussion reviewed GrowthBook’s capabilities for experiment visibility, cross-platform measurement, data architecture, configuration, and analytics. Its timeline supports concurrent experiment review through project, metric, and tag filters, but collision detection across shared populations or attributes remains unresolved and requires manual review. Warehouse joins can connect backend or scoring-service exposure with mobile outcomes, provided consistent identity mapping and queryable events are available. The warehouse remains the source of truth, with assignment data requiring an identifier, experiment ID, evaluation key, and timestamp. GrowthBook supports feature flags, targeting, staged rollouts, guardrail metrics, multiple variants, reusable templates, Bayesian analysis, historical experiment analysis, dashboards, and learning workflows. The team is completing the warehouse connection and security approval, plans to begin with direct A/B testing, and expects results in approximately one month. Enterprise access lasts two weeks, creating a risk if it expires before launch. Success criteria remain undefined.

## Keywords
GrowthBook POC, A/B experimentation, Feature flags, Cross-platform metrics, Snowflake data warehouse, Experiment analytics
